draftArchitecture.openingJob: Explain who sued whom and what subscription value they allege was lost, then immediately identify the claim as unproven.
causalSequence: Plaintiffs say an agreement among competing providers to slow development would diminish what they bought.
They distinguish an alleged shared restraint from each company taking its own safety precautions.
They ask a court for relief; filing does not supply the judgment.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: Distinguish a company delaying its own release after testing from competitors agreeing to restrain development; do not claim either hypothetical proves this case.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: If another subscription lawsuit is announced, ask what the filing alleges, what evidence supports it, and what the court has actually decided.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Understand the stage of the dispute; no account cancellation, refund entitlement or legal advice follows from filing alone.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes; Sources.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No battle framing between safety and consumer rights, no technical-work assumptions, no personal advice to join the case.

humourPlan.noneReason: The distinction between an allegation and a ruling needs a clear opening; no decorative courtroom joke.

readerQuestions.question: Who filed and what do they allege?
Does the complaint oppose all safety work?
Has a court established wrongdoing or granted relief?

draftArchitecture.presentationPlan: The admitted people-free editorial image shows a complaint under examination and four separate unbranded subscription receipts. It must not imply a verdict, proven coordination, brand identity or a court order.
draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Subscribers have alleged unlawful coordination over an AI slowdown; the filing does not establish that allegation or change readers’ accounts.
